newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch hope EU will relax curbs on pig exports.
newsitem.headline: Dutch hope EU will relax curbs on pig exports.

text.p: The Netherlands is hoping the European Union will decide on Wednesday to relax an export ban on live pigs following an outbreak of swine fever which threatens a $2.7 billion a year export industry.
EU veterinary experts are meeting in Brussels today to review measures the Dutch have taken to contain and eradicate the highly contagious disease, which is not harmful to humans.
"Obviously we hope the veterinary committee will recommend a relaxation of the measures, but it is impossible to predict the outcome," Farm Ministry spokesman Ton van der Molen said.
EU farm inspectors have conducted a three-day inspection in the southern province of Brabant where the disease broke out and are due to report their findings to the committee today.
Dutch officials will also report on the latest measures taken to halt the spread of the virus.
In the most dramatic development to date, the government said on Monday it would buy and destroy 800,000 pigs which cannot be marketed because of a ban on transporting livestock.
The European Union will meet some 70 percent of the cost, estimated at 150 million guilders ($80 million).

Since the first case was confirmed on February 4, swine fever has been detected on 18 farms in Brabant. All but one fall within an area of the province containing roughly one fifth of the country's 14 million pigs.
Some 35,000 pigs from infected or neighbouring farms have already been destroyed and transport of any kind of livestock has been banned in a 10 km (six mile) radius of those farms.
Pig markets have been closed in the whole of the country to prevent the infection spreading.
Last week the EU slapped a ban on the export of live pigs from the Netherlands, except the four northernmost provinces.
Farm Minister Jozias van Aartsen condemned this as a "panic measure", given the limited distribution of the disease.
The U.S. had already halted imports of Dutch pork products and Poland had closed its borders to Dutch pigs and pork.
In 1996 the Netherlands exported almost a million tonnes of pigs and pork products, about 60 percent of its production, bringing in around 5.1 billion guilders ($2.7 billion).
Germany is the main foreign market for Dutch pigs and pork products taking 38 percent of all Dutch exports, followed by Italy (22 percent), Britain (11 percent) and France (eight percent).
